title: API-access credential administration: first-party hashed API keys (Q-19) with reveal-once/regenerate/disable
objective: Implement the approved Q-19 first-party API-key scheme's admin surface: create (reveal-once), regenerate, and disable tenant- and broker-scoped intake credentials stored as salted hashes in api_credentials, preserving the existing admin UX contract and audit semantics (Q-19, P-04 API-access admin).
scope: Credential endpoints per the reference ApiAccess contract: list, create (returns plaintext key exactly once), regenerate (new key, old invalidated, reveal-once), disable — tenant-scoped and broker-scoped variants

Key generation + verification module: cryptographically random keys with a public lookup prefix (key_id) and salted hash (+ env pepper API_KEY_PEPPER); constant-time comparison; verify-only (never retrievable)
Audit: credential create/regenerate/disable/last-used semantics per reference
The verification function is exported for T-030 (intake auth)
out_of_scope: Supabase Vault (explicitly not used for these keys per Q-19/Q-23)
implementation_details: Key format: prefix (identifiable, e.g., qiq_) + key_id + secret; store key_id plaintext for lookup, hash(secret + salt + pepper) via a Node crypto primitive (scrypt or sha256-HMAC per security review — no custom crypto, standard library only).
Reveal-once: plaintext appears solely in the create/regenerate response; responses and logs never contain it elsewhere; audit rows store key_id only.
Regenerate atomically swaps hash and rotation metadata; disabled credentials fail verification immediately.
Broker-scoped credentials carry broker_id; tenant resolution during verification comes from the credential row (unspoofable, P-06).
verifyApiKey(presentedKey) -> Result<CredentialContext{tenantId, brokerId?, credentialId}> with timing-safe comparisons and no user enumeration in errors.

unit: Key generation entropy/format; hash+verify roundtrip; wrong key fails; pepper change invalidates verification; constant-time comparison used
integration: Create returns plaintext once; subsequent list/get never exposes it; DB stores only hashes
Regenerate invalidates the old key and the new one verifies; disable stops verification
Broker-scoped credential resolves its broker; tenant isolation on credential admin; audit rows for all lifecycle events
Permission matrix on the admin endpoints
e2e: API-access settings spec adapted in T-043

findings.title: The unknown-key timing decoy has no coverage; add a deterministic structural pin
findings.detail: REPRODUCED FIRST-HAND: deleting the equalizeUnknownKeyTiming call from verifyApiKey (service.ts 358->357 lines, sha b2287->altered, restored byte-identical to b2287) leaves all 59 tests green. The implementor's disposition — record NO COVERAGE rather than fake a flaky statistical timing test — is CORRECT and is hereby ratified; a wall-clock timing assertion in CI would be noise. However, the codebase already has the precedent for a DETERMINISTIC structural pin: api-keys.test.ts:151-157 asserts keys.ts calls timingSafeEqual by reading the shipped source. The same one-assertion pattern (assert service.ts invokes equalizeUnknownKeyTiming on the unknown-key path) would have killed this mutant at zero flake cost. NON-BLOCKING recommendation: add the structural pin in T-030 (which consumes verifyApiKey and will re-assert the 401 mapping at the HTTP boundary) or fold into the next touch of this suite. No statistical timing test is wanted.

history.message: Task generated by Planner from approved spec.md. Maps to Q-19, P-04 API-access admin, section 13 intake auth.

Implemented the Q-19 first-party hashed API-key admin surface test-first. Files created: src/server/domains/api-access/{keys,schemas,errors,repository,service,routes,index}.ts; src/server/tests/unit/api-keys.test.ts (23 tests); src/server/tests/integration/api-access.test.ts (36 tests). Shared files touched: src/server/lib/router/app.ts (apiAccess slot + route registration), api/v1/[[...segments]].ts and scripts/dev/serve-api.ts (defaultApiAccessDeps(config)), src/server/tests/integration/auth-wiring.test.ts (composition-root pin, which also pins the (config) argument). No schema change: 20260718002400_api_credentials.sql already shipped key_id/key_hash/key_salt, and API_KEY_PEPPER was already in the typed config schema and both env example files as placeholders. RED OBSERVED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION: both suites failed with 'Cannot find module ../../domains/api-access/...' before any production file existed. GATES (serial, isolated): own suites 87/87 exit 0; typecheck 0 errors; scoped lint 0 and repo-wide `eslint .` 0; db:types:check 'Generated DB types are up to date'. RESIDUE: suite run from a clean baseline leaves 0 tenants/credentials/audit rows/brokers (verified by direct DB query). One earlier leak of 16 tenants was self-inflicted — a `--reporter=verbose | head -20` run was SIGPIPE-killed before afterAll ran; the orphans were removed and the clean-baseline re-run confirmed zero.

MEASURED vs ASSUMED, three contradictions recorded rather than silently resolved. (1) BASE PATH: V-051 names `POST /api/v1/api-credentials`; the reference group is `/api/v1/settings/api-credentials` (ApiAccessEndpoints.cs:33) and the SPA calls that path (settingsApi.ts:301-322). Implemented the MEASURED path; the verification-plan path would 404 the Settings API-access tab and the broker API section. (2) LIST ENVELOPE: this domain's list is a bare `{credentials: [...]}` (ApiAccessDtos.cs:42), NOT the house `{items,totalCount,page,pageSize}`. There is at most one credential per scope, so there is nothing to page; the standing `totalCount` lesson does NOT apply here and applying it would break the tab. (3) PERMISSIONS: the task file speaks generally of admin endpoints; the reference uses four granular codes (api_access.view/enable/disable/regenerate_secret), all already seeded and in the permission catalog, and the SPA already references all four. Used those, no new code added.

FOUR DECISIONS FLAGGED FOR EVALUATOR RULING, not silently filled. (1) THE REVEAL ENDPOINT. The reference's POST /{id}/reveal re-served the secret via a live Keycloak call; under Q-19 the stored form is a salted hash and the migration header states the reveal path 'has no successor and must not grow one'. The SPA still calls it. Chosen: keep the route REGISTERED behind its original api_access.view guard and answer 410 with code API_CREDENTIAL_NOT_REVEALABLE, because a bare 404 is indistinguishable from a wiring bug and the T-043 e2e needs a deterministic answer. Explicitly REJECTED: aliasing reveal to regenerate, which would rotate a live integration's key on a read-looking click (pinned by a test asserting the key hash is unchanged and the old key still verifies after a reveal attempt). Open product question: should T-043 remove the 'Reveal secret' button? (2) DISABLED CREDENTIALS BLOCK RE-PROVISIONING. The reference's existence check does not filter on status, so a disabled credential permanently occupies its scope; combined with the SPA (which shows a disabled credential with no buttons and never re-offers 'Enable API access'), this is a dead end. Preserved for contract parity and flagged rather than 'fixed', because relaxing it changes what unique-per-scope means for intake. (3) HASH CHOICE. HMAC-SHA-256 over `${salt}:${secret}` with an env pepper, not scrypt. Rationale: the secret is 32 bytes of randomBytes (256 bits uniformly random), so it is not brute-forceable regardless of hash speed; scrypt exists to compensate for low-entropy human secrets and its cost would be paid on every intake request in a serverless runtime. The migration header explicitly anticipated either ('scrypt or sha256-HMAC per security review'). One place to overrule: keys.ts hashApiKeySecret. (4) THE `name` COLUMN. NOT NULL in the schema but absent from the reference DTO and from the SPA; populated with a derived label ('Tenant API key' / 'Broker {id} API key') rather than inventing a request field.

TEN MUTANTS, each PROVEN APPLIED with a proof matched to its shape (sha256 prefix delta for same-line edits, line-count delta for deletions) and each restored byte-identically (restore proof = sha256 returning to the pre-mutation value). git diff is blind here: src/server/domains/api-access/ was a new untracked directory. NINE KILLED: M1 drop the salt from the hash message (keys.ts, sha c157->c790, 147 lines, 2 unit tests failed); M2 ignore the pepper (sha c157->da3a, 1 unit + 1 integration failed); M3 delete the disabled-credential guard in verifyApiKey (service.ts, 359->357 lines, killed 'disable stops verification'); M4a/M4b the required STATUS-vs-CODE discrimination pair on invalidBrokerError — 422->400 with the code intact (sha 49df->0499) and code->API_CREDENTIAL_VALIDATION_FAILED with 422 intact (sha 49df->81e3) BOTH killed the same two tests, proving the assertions discriminate status and code independently rather than either alone; M5 drop the tenant predicate from findCredential (repository.ts, sha fb74->ab7b, killed both cross-tenant no-side-effect tests); M6 delete the already-exists guard (service.ts, 359->355 lines); M7 weaken the regenerate guard to api_access.view (routes.ts, sha f8f4->e097, 4 tests); M8 turn the reveal 410 into a 200 no-op (sha f8f4->29e5); M9 make recordApiKeyUse a no-op (sha b228->01e8). ONE SURVIVOR, HONESTLY CLAIMED AS NO COVERAGE: M10 deleted equalizeUnknownKeyTiming — the decoy HMAC on the unknown-key path (service.ts, 359->358 lines) — and all 59 tests stayed green. This is NOT equivalent code: without it, response time distinguishes a valid key id from an invalid one and the constant-time comparison downstream protects nothing. It is untestable deterministically (a timing assertion is flaky in CI), so it is recorded as UNCOVERED rather than covered by a weakened test. Evaluator input welcome on whether a statistical timing test is wanted. NOTE: M3's first restore was BOTCHED — reversing a deletion by replacing the empty string reinserted the guard at the top of the file — and the sha proof caught it (b228 expected, bd43 observed). The file was repaired to the byte-identical original (sha b228, 359 lines), the helper was rewritten to restore from a snapshot rather than by reversing the replacement, and M3 was re-run cleanly. This is exactly the failure mode a status-only or diff-only proof would have missed.

Plaintext key exists in exactly two places: a local variable in provisionCredential/regenerateSecret and the response body those two return. Never persisted, never logged, never in an audit payload (audit rows carry clientId — the public key id — plus brokerId and status only), never re-derivable. Asserted by scanning EVERY text column of the stored row and the serialized audit details for both the full key and its secret half, not by spot-checking key_hash. Node standard-library crypto only (createHmac/randomBytes/timingSafeEqual), no new dependencies, no custom crypto. timingSafeEqual is guarded against the length mismatch it throws on, so a truncated key_hash is an ordinary auth failure rather than a 500 that would confirm the row exists. verifyApiKey returns one opaque message for all four failure reasons (malformed_key/unknown_key/credential_disabled/secret_mismatch are for server-side logging only) so no user or tenant enumeration is possible; T-030 must map all of them to one identical 401. Tenant during verification comes from the credential row itself (the single deliberate cross-partition read, which asserts exactly one match rather than taking the first). The pepper reaches the domain only as a parameter from defaultApiAccessDeps(config) — keys.ts and service.ts never touch process.env. verifyApiKey and recordApiKeyUse are exported from domains/api-access/index.js for T-030.

T-024 (leads backend core) ran concurrently against the same local database. Mid-run typechecks showed transient errors in src/server/domains/leads/repository.ts (insertInto arity, numeric-vs-string column types) that are NOT this task's files; by the final gate run they were resolved and typecheck/lint were both 0 repo-wide. Nothing in leads was touched. db:validate and supabase:reset were NOT run (destructive on the shared DB, per the coordination rules); the ci:test floor was NOT touched — the orchestrator owns it after all parallel tasks land. The shared-file pass (router slot, both composition roots, auth-wiring pin) was done last in one pass with a re-read immediately before each edit; every edit applied on the first attempt, and the sibling's leads wiring appeared in app.ts alongside mine without conflict.

VERDICT: PASS (iteration 0). RULINGS ON THE FIVE ESCALATED POINTS, each verified against the reference first-hand, not taken from the implementor's report. (1) BASE PATH + LIST ENVELOPE: both deviations RATIFIED. ApiAccessEndpoints.cs:33 reads TenantScopedGroup("/api/v1/settings/api-credentials") and ApiCredentialListDto (ApiAccessDtos.cs, 'record ApiCredentialListDto(IReadOnlyList<ApiCredentialDto> Credentials)') is a bare {credentials:[...]} — read directly from the reference source by the evaluator. The measured contract wins over both the verification plan and the orchestrator's totalCount generalisation; V-051's endpoint paths have been corrected in .claude/verification.json (evaluator-owned metadata) so T-043's e2e targets real routes. AC-045-style amendment is NOT needed here because AC-040's text names no path. (2) REVEAL 410: RATIFIED. The reference reveal re-served the secret live from Keycloak (CredentialSecretDto doc comment confirms); the migration header (20260718002400:41-42) states the path 'has no successor and must not grow one', and spec Q-19 says 'plaintext keys shown reveal-once only'. 410 API_CREDENTIAL_NOT_REVEALABLE behind the original api_access.view guard is the correct answer: distinguishable from a wiring 404, non-enumerating (guard runs first, and a nonsense id still 404s), and the refusal to alias reveal->regenerate is right — a state-rotating side effect behind a read-looking click would silently break live integrations; the no-rotation property is pinned by a test the evaluator read (api-access.test.ts:674-690). The SPA's 'Reveal secret' button IS T-043's problem: recommend T-043 remove it or replace it with an explicit Regenerate flow carrying a destructive-action confirmation. (3) DISABLED-CREDENTIAL SCOPE BLOCKING: RATIFIED as parity. FindTenantCredentialAsync/FindBrokerCredentialAsync (ApiCredentialStore.cs:51-63) verifiably carry no status filter. Preserving the dead end and flagging it is correct for a migration; changing unique-per-scope semantics belongs to a deliberate product decision, recommended as a small follow-up task (allow re-provision of a disabled scope OR add an enable path), not a silent 'fix'. (4) HMAC-SHA-256 OVER SCRYPT: RATIFIED as a security decision. The secret is 32 bytes of randomBytes (256 bits, uniform); memory-hard KDFs exist to protect low-entropy human secrets, and their cost here would be paid on every intake request in a serverless runtime. Salt defeats cross-row correlation, env pepper (never in the DB) defeats offline verification against a dump, and the migration header explicitly anticipated this choice. This is the industry-standard construction for machine API keys. (5) M10 SURVIVOR: reproduced first-hand (see finding T-022-F1) — disposition ratified, honest no-coverage over a weakened or flaky test; a deterministic structural pin is recommended, no statistical timing test. SECURITY PROPERTIES VERIFIED FIRST-HAND: plaintext exists only as locals in provisionCredential/regenerateSecret and their response bodies; tests scan EVERY text column of the stored row and serialized audit details for both the full key and its secret half (not just key_hash); zero logger/console/process.env references in the domain (grep); pepper flows only through defaultApiAccessDeps(config.secrets.apiKeyPepper); both env example files carry angle-bracket placeholders; timingSafeEqual with an explicit length guard so a corrupted hash is a 401 not a 500; one opaque failure message for all four reasons; verification tenant comes from the credential row via findCredentialByKeyId, which asserts exactly-one-match and is unreachable from admin routes. verifyApiKey SEAM FOR T-030: sound — Result<CredentialContext{credentialId,tenantId,brokerId}, ApiKeyVerificationFailure{reason,message}> with reasons for server-side logging only and an identical message across all four, so T-030 can (and must) map every failure to one identical 401; recordApiKeyUse is separate and non-authorizing, verified pure-read by test. GATES RE-RUN BY THE EVALUATOR, SERIAL: own suites 59/59; parties+auth-wiring 98/98; typecheck 0; lint 0 (repo-wide eslint, which also proves the no-restricted-properties AC-010 gate); db:types:check clean; FULL suite 71 files / 1473 passed / exit 0, matching the orchestrator's floor. MUTANTS RE-RUN FIRST-HAND: M10 (survivor confirmed, restore sha-verified b2287...); the orchestrator's env-scan fix proven with all three mutants on keys.ts (plain read caught, trailing-comment read caught, comment-only mention ignored; keys.ts restored byte-identical sha c1574...). Taken on trust from the implementor's report (spot-checked consistent, not re-executed): M1-M9's individual kill runs and the RED-before-implementation observation.
